name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,816

entries.clue: Story of unfair dismissal had hippie all worked up (12)

indicatorNotes.worked up: letters worked up are stirred into a new order

annotation.surface: A hippie sacked without cause is furious about it.
annotation.walkthrough: Philadelphia is the 1993 film in which Tom Hanks plays a lawyer fired for having AIDS, so the definition is a cryptic description of its plot, not of the city.
annotation.definitionFit: The film Philadelphia tells the story of a lawyer's unfair dismissal.

entries.clue: Operation in sub (3,11)

blocks.note: a sub is a substitute, a replacement

annotation.surface: Something happening aboard a submarine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Operation in sub' reads like a naval mission; both small words must be swapped for synonyms, 'in' as trendy and 'sub' as a stand-in player.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition by category: the answer names one particular kind of surgical operation.

entries.clue: Friend given a raise celebrated, making tea (7)

indicatorNotes.given a raise: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upwards, reading bottom to top

annotation.surface: A friend got a pay rise, celebrated, and put the kettle on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Given a raise' sounds like a pay rise, but in a down answer it lifts PAL to read LAP. Lapsang souchong is a smoky Chinese tea.
annotation.definitionFit: Lapsang (souchong) is a variety of smoked black tea.

entries.clue: Daughters in education took courses (5)

annotation.surface: Daughters at school took classes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Took courses' suggests study, matching the education in the surface; the courses are the parts of a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: To have dined is to have eaten a meal of several courses.

entries.clue: Back from Chernobyl in the morning, criminal's glowing (7)

indicatorNotes.Back from: the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: bent = criminal, corrupt; the 's is 'is', joining to the definition

annotation.surface: Someone back from Chernobyl is glowing with radiation by the next morning.
annotation.walkthrough: The radioactive picture makes 'glowing' look literal; the answer is a softer, literary glow.
annotation.definitionFit: Lambent means softly glowing or flickering, as of a flame or light.

entries.clue: Crew feathers easily (5,4)

annotation.surface: A crew rowing or feathering oars with ease.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feathers' looks like a verb, as in feathering an oar, and 'crew' like rowers; both are nouns here.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom, from horse racing: a jockey so far ahead he could drop his hands and loosen the reins won without effort.

entries.clue: In danger while pinching Tesla on drive (2,5)

indicatorNotes.pinching: AS pinches T, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the second

blocks.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
take = drive, as in 'I'll take you to the station'

annotation.surface: Stealing a Tesla to drive it puts you in danger.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, which fits 'pinching' and 'drive'; it is the unit, abbreviated T.
annotation.definitionFit: Something at stake is at risk, in danger of being lost.

entries.clue: Furiously making kid suffer? (4-3-7)

blocks.note: the straight sense: going flat out, at a furious pace
not a child: kid is soft goatskin, and making it suffer means putting that material through torment

annotation.surface: Someone angrily torments a child.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Furiously' is the plain meaning; the rest reads the phrase literally, since kid is a fine leather, so making kid suffer is putting leather through hell.
annotation.definitionFit: Hell-for-leather means at breakneck speed, furiously.

entries.clue: Nurse gets hose inserted for shock treatment (6)

indicatorNotes.inserted: something inserted is pushed inside something else, so PIPE goes into EN

blocks.note: a hose is a flexible pipe

annotation.surface: A nurse administers a hosepipe as a form of shock treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shock treatment' suggests electroconvulsive therapy; the shock is anaphylactic, and an EpiPen is the adrenaline injector used for it.
annotation.definitionFit: An EpiPen injects adrenaline to treat anaphylactic shock.

entries.clue: Very short and severe cut for priest (8)

indicatorNotes.cut: STERN is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: mini = very short, as in a miniskirt
STERN (severe) cut of its last letter

annotation.surface: A barber's order: a very short, severe haircut for the priest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Severe cut' reads as a harsh haircut; 'cut' is an instruction to clip STERN.
annotation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, a priest or pastor.

entries.clue: Royal costume changing hands anyway (10)

indicatorNotes.changing hands: the hands are L (left) and R (right), which swap places

annotation.surface: A royal outfit passes to a new owner all the same.
annotation.walkthrough: REGALDRESS has one L and one R; swapping those two letters, left for right, gives REGARDLESS.
annotation.definitionFit: Regardless means anyway, in spite of everything.

entries.clue: Beer bottles by bar spinning? (4)

indicatorNotes.bottles: ALE bottles X, holding it inside

blocks.note: x = by, as in 3 x 4 ('three by four')

annotation.surface: Beer bottles lined up by a bar, maybe spinning to the drinker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, in keeping with beer; it is a rod, and the question mark flags that an axle is a bar that spins, or that wheels spin on.
annotation.definitionFit: An axle is a rod on which wheels turn.

entries.clue: Book something you'd burn with job writing on-line (8)

blocks.note: a log goes on the fire

annotation.surface: A book to burn, with a job writing lines as punishment.
annotation.walkthrough: The book burning and 'writing on-line' feel like a punishment of lines; the definition is a piece published on the internet.
annotation.definitionFit: A blog post is a piece of writing published online.

entries.clue: Old man at home cuts open coat again (9)

indicatorNotes.cuts open: PA IN cuts OVERT open, splitting it apart

annotation.surface: A father at home slices open a coat to recycle it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cuts open' looks like one phrase meaning slices; 'cuts' is the insertion, and 'open' is OVERT.
annotation.definitionFit: To overpaint is to cover with a fresh coat of paint.

entries.clue: Cat turned green by random drawing (6)

indicatorNotes.turned: ECO is turned round to read OCE

blocks.note: a lot is drawn at random to decide something

annotation.surface: A cat turned green in a child's random drawing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Random drawing' paints a picture; here it means a lot, as in drawing lots.
annotation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of the Americas.

entries.clue: Coffee shop feeds me business cleaning drives etc. (6)

indicatorNotes.feeds: to feed is to put food into a mouth, so CAFE is put into ME

blocks.note: a cafe is a coffee shop

annotation.surface: A coffee shop that feeds me also cleans driveways.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cleaning drives' suggests driveways or car valeting; the drives are computer disk drives, and McAfee sells antivirus software.
annotation.definitionFit: McAfee is a company whose antivirus software cleans computer drives of malware.

entries.clue: Doctor's tool meant to be used on fungal growths (7)

blocks.note: for = intended for, meant to be used on

annotation.surface: A doctor's instrument is meant for treating fungal infections.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'fungal growths' sound like an infection; ceps are wild mushrooms.
annotation.definitionFit: Forceps are pincers used by surgeons and doctors.

entries.clue: Story on X about Conservative grasping organ (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, TALE goes on after TEN
indicatorNotes.about: TALE goes about C, around it

blocks.note: X is ten in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A news story posted on X about a Tory with a grasping nature.
annotation.walkthrough: X looks like the social network, fitting 'story' and 'Conservative'; it is the Roman numeral ten.
annotation.definitionFit: A tentacle is a flexible limb used for grasping.

entries.clue: Sportsmen seeing irritable bull coming over? (7)

indicatorNotes.coming over: the letters come over, turning upside down in a down answer

annotation.surface: Bullfighters see an angry bull charging at them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bull' in a bullfighting picture is the animal; here it means nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Toreros are bullfighters, loosely called sportsmen.

entries.clue: Determined US lawyer Ray gets back up (7)

indicatorNotes.gets back up: in a down answer, the back letter moves up to the top

blocks.note: DA = district attorney, an American prosecutor
a manta is a large ray

annotation.surface: A resolute American lawyer called Ray gets out of bed again.
annotation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a man's name; it is the fish. DAMANTA's final A climbs to the top to give ADAMANT.
annotation.definitionFit: Adamant means determined, refusing to be moved.

entries.clue: Queen holds reversible one metre ruler (4)

indicatorNotes.holds: whatever holds something has it in its grip, so ER wraps round MI
indicatorNotes.reversible: a reversible thing can be turned round, like a reversible coat, so IM becomes MI

annotation.surface: The Queen owns a two-sided metre rule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Metre ruler' looks like a measuring stick; the ruler is the definition, a Muslim prince.
annotation.definitionFit: An emir is a ruler in parts of the Muslim world.

entries.clue: Notice each boy twice (8,2)

indicatorNotes.twice: twice means do it two times, so 'each boy' is read two times with different synonyms

blocks.note: a = each, as in 'two pounds a head'

annotation.surface: Tell each boy twice so he takes notice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twice' tells you to use 'each boy' two times with different synonyms: PER SON, then A LAD.
annotation.definitionFit: A personal ad is a notice placed in a newspaper, often seeking a partner.

entries.clue: President entertained by dream about going to heaven (5)

indicatorNotes.entertained by: the answer is held inside the next words
indicatorNotes.going to heaven: in a down answer, going up to heaven reverses the letters

annotation.surface: A president has a religious dream about the afterlife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a reversal indicator; the letters are simply hidden across 'dream about' and read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Barack Obama held the office of US President from 2009 to 2017.

entries.clue: Westerly parts of Ireland entered by priest regularly, up-country (8)

indicatorNotes.Westerly: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left
indicatorNotes.entered by: RET enters between the two parts
indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters of priest are taken at every second place

annotation.surface: A priest regularly visits the west of Ireland, far inland.
annotation.walkthrough: The two parts of Ireland are its two jurisdictions, abbreviated ROI and NI; with RET between them, the whole reads westward.
annotation.definitionFit: Up-country means in the interior, away from the coast.

entries.clue: Lack of care, making a burger's ultimate temperature hot (6)

indicatorNotes.making: the change is being made to the burger
indicatorNotes.hot: 'temperature hot' reads as a temperature turning hot, so T (temperature) turns into H (hot)

blocks.note: the last T (temperature) of PATTY becomes H (hot)

annotation.surface: Carelessness means a burger ends up overcooked.
annotation.walkthrough: The burger picture makes 'temperature hot' sound like cooking; the last T of PATTY is swapped for H.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: apathy is not caring about anything, from the Greek for without feeling.

entries.clue: Thrashing a fascist right-winger is OK (12)

indicatorNotes.Thrashing: the letters of A FASCIST are beaten into a new shape

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

annotation.surface: Someone says beating a fascist right-winger is fine.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a political argument; 'thrashing' is only telling you to scramble A FASCIST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something OK is good enough, which is what satisfactory grades say.
